titles: “WHAT DO YOU EXPECT ME TO DO?” Eddie Hearn FIRES BACK at Dana White Over Fury-Joshua
“PR DISASTERS” Eddie Hearn BLASTS Dana White as Fury-Joshua PROMOTION ERUPTS
“IF HE LANDS THE RIGHT HAND, THIS FIGHT'S OVER” Carl Froch WARNS Tyson Fury
“COMING TOGETHER ON DECEMBER 11TH” Carl Froch CONFIRMS Fury-Joshua Cardiff Showdown
“I'M WITH TYSON” Frank Warren BACKS Fury and DISMISSES the Joshua Fight Negativity

blocks.narration: Meanwhile, Eddie Hearn opens the Fury-Joshua story by explaining why the promotion has turned ugly around Dana White and the December 11 fight. He frames the video’s central question: who actually controlled the launch in London?

On the other side, Eddie Hearn points toward a public-relations collapse for Dana White’s side after the September 30 press conference. He says the dispute became a major problem during the week that Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally faced each other.

At the same time, Eddie Hearn lays out his version of White’s position at the event. He says White could have attended as a spectator, while warning that the disagreement may create more Matchroom and Zuffa battles later.
Beyond that, Tyson Fury fires back at the argument over who should promote the fight. He says Turki Alalshikh, who is funding the event, can involve Dana White or any promoter he chooses.

Adding to that, Tyson Fury keeps the Hearn-White feud separate from his own assignment against Anthony Joshua. He presents the dispute as an issue between the promoters rather than something affecting his preparation for Cardiff.

Taking that further, Tyson Fury questions Eddie Hearn’s suggestion that he fears Joshua. He calls Hearn a nuisance and reduces the December 11 event to a professional boxing job between two heavyweights.

On a similar note, Tyson Fury weighs in on Anthony Joshua’s reunion with Ben Davison. He argues that Joshua previously left Davison because he was not good enough, making the trainer’s return part of the pre-fight argument.

From Eddie Hearn’s side, the promoter highlights the tension that could have emerged if he had been placed between the two fighters. He says Tyson Fury would not want Hearn provoking both men during the press conference.

However, John Fury questions the explanation surrounding Peter Fury’s contact with Anthony Joshua. He argues that general advice would make little sense unless Joshua wanted information about Tyson Fury himself.

That's when John Fury attacks Ben Davison’s position in the story. He says Tyson Fury gave Davison his biggest opportunity and views Davison’s work with Anthony Joshua as a direct betrayal before the Cardiff fight.

Then, John Fury puts his own loyalty forward as the standard for judging Peter Fury’s involvement. He says even a billion-dollar offer would not persuade him to help Anthony Joshua prepare specifically for Tyson.

Meanwhile, Frank Warren questions what Anthony Joshua’s search for outside input says about his mindset. He points to the return to Ben Davison and the Peter Fury link as signs that Joshua may be seeking reassurance.

On the other side, Dominic Ingle reveals another interpretation of Joshua speaking with Peter Fury and Ben Davison. He compares the situation with fighters looking for inside information instead of relying entirely on their own ability.

At the same time, Dominic Ingle keeps loyalty in the conversation by focusing on the trainer-fighter relationship. He suggests that poor pay can weaken loyalty, even when a coach has previously worked closely with an opponent.

Beyond that, Carl Froch questions Anthony Joshua’s recent form before the biggest fight of his career. He describes Joshua as being near the end of his run after a damaging performance against a lesser-regarded opponent.

Adding to that, Carl Froch picks Tyson Fury despite acknowledging that Fury is no longer as sharp as he once was. He says Fury’s natural ability remains enough to make him the favorite against Joshua.

Taking that further, Carl Froch weighs in on the Hearn-White argument after White missed the London launch. He sees Eddie Hearn as having gained the upper hand because the fight ultimately landed in Britain.

On a similar note, Carl Froch highlights what the London face-off confirmed about the event itself. He says Fury and Joshua are now scheduled to meet on December 11, with Cardiff providing the setting for the showdown.

From Carl Froch’s side, the former champion points toward the legacy stakes for both heavyweights. He says the fight offers closure over who was the better British heavyweight, while noting that both careers already include major defeats.
However, Carl Froch puts Anthony Joshua’s most dangerous route forward in simple terms. He says Joshua may be able to end the fight if he lands his right hand cleanly against Tyson Fury.

That's when Frank Warren doubles down on Tyson Fury’s side of the rivalry. He says he has no personal animosity toward Anthony Joshua, but makes clear that his support remains with Fury ahead of December 11.

Then, John Fury weighs in on the judging pressure surrounding the matchup. He argues that Anthony Joshua has the British crowd and environment behind him, while claiming Tyson Fury may need a knockout to secure the result.

outro: Eddie Hearn and Tyson Fury dismiss each other’s sides of the promotional dispute, while the Peter Fury link and Ben Davison reunion add a separate layer of tension around Anthony Joshua. With both fighters’ reputations and late-career legacies on the line, what happens next could reshape the British heavyweight division. So, drop your thoughts below.
description:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are set to meet on December 11 in Cardiff after their September 30 London launch produced clashes over Dana White, Eddie Hearn, billing, and the promotion of the fight.

The latest controversy also involves Anthony Joshua’s return to Ben Davison and reports that he spoke with Tyson Fury’s uncle, Peter Fury. John Fury, Frank Warren, Dominic Ingle, Carl Froch, Eddie Hearn, and Tyson Fury all offer different views on the fallout.

Credits: The Stomping Ground, Boxing News, Playbook Boxing, Boxing King Media, Froch On Fighting.
pinned_comment: Who has the stronger edge going into Cardiff: Tyson Fury with his experience, or Anthony Joshua with Ben Davison and the Peter Fury connection?
